item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Portrait From a Seventies Film

turns.text: Make this look like a still from a 1970s movie—warm faded colours and film grain. Keep her recognisable and keep the square framing. No text.

item.tests: Applies a convincing 1970s film treatment while preserving the uploaded portrait's identity and composition.

answer_sheet.Style and mood: A nostalgic 1970s colour film still, with warm faded colours and visible film grain.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: Her identity, curly dark hair, sweater, pose and park setting.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One square image; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The woman remains recognisable as the woman in the source portrait.
Her curly dark hair, sweater and head-and-shoulders framing are retained.
The park background remains identifiable rather than becoming a different setting.
Warm, faded colour grading and visible film grain give the image a 1970s film-still appearance.
The output is square and contains no added text.

turns.text: Could you make this pic look like a still from a 1970s movie? I’ve always had a soft spot for the way old movies feel like memories. Please keep her recognisable and keep the square framing. I’m thinking warm faded colours and film grain for that movie look. I’m excited to see how this photo feels with that bit of nostalgia. No text, please.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Restyle this portrait as a naturalistic still from a 1970s colour movie, with the intimate nostalgic feeling of a warm faded memory. Preserve the woman's exact identity and recognizable facial features, expression, dark curly hair, gray knitted sweater, pose, and park setting. Preserve the original square framing and subject scale. Apply warm, gently faded analogue film colours, muted olive greens, soft amber highlights, slightly lifted blacks, restrained contrast, fine visible organic 35mm film grain, subtle halation and gentle optical softness. Keep natural skin texture and faithful facial proportions; no face redesign, no beautification. Photographic, understated cinematic colour grading rather than an illustration. No text, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, borders or letterboxing.
